ECE 6390 / Spacecraft systems

Solar array

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how orientation, temperature and aging affect useful solar-array power.

A flat front-illuminated panel intercepts solar power proportional to projected area A max(0, cos α), where α is the angle between the panel normal and sunlight. Normal incidence maximizes the intercepted power.

The model multiplies intercepted power by reference cell efficiency, a temperature factor, an end-of-life factor, and bus efficiency: P = SAηref max(0, cos α)[1 + aT(T − Tref)]fEOLfbus.

Keep each factor attached to its physical role and apply it once. The supplied temperature and degradation coefficients illustrate a model; a particular cell or mission needs its own measured coefficients and illumination history.

Example

At reference temperature before aging and bus losses, a 1 m² panel with 30% efficiency under 1,361 W/m² illumination produces 408.3 W at normal incidence and 204.2 W at 60°.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. With all other factors unchanged, how much additional panel area compensates for moving from normal incidence to 60°?

    The cosine factor falls from 1 to 1/2.

    Twice the area restores the same modeled power, provided the added area has the same illumination, temperature, cell efficiency, and downstream losses.
